lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Welcome! I'm Tilly, and I collect <color=red>stories</color> the way other people collect coins.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Read this one closely, then answer four questions. Get them all right and four new <color=red>books</color> will find their way onto the library shelves.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Odalys had spent forty years as a <color=red>cartographer</color>, drawing maps of coastlines no one else had dared to chart. Her final commission was the most <color=red>treacherous</color> yet: the Whispering Isles.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Fog clung to the water, and her compass spun uselessly. Rather than panic, she studied the <color=red>patterns</color> of the gulls, which always flew toward land at dusk.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: By following the birds, she found a hidden channel between the rocks. When she finally sketched it, she wrote beneath it: "Trust what you observe, not only what you were taught."

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: The map was never sold. Odalys hung it in her workshop, where apprentices came to learn that careful <color=red>observation</color> can succeed where instruments fail.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 1: Why was the final commission described as <color=red>treacherous</color>?
choices: It had to be finished quickly
lines.hint: Not quite. Reread how the first part describes the Whispering Isles.
lines.correctText: Correct. The waters were dangerous and uncharted.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 2: How did Odalys find the hidden channel?
lines.hint: Not quite. Her compass was no use in the fog.
lines.correctText: Yes. The gulls always flew toward land at dusk.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 3: What lesson does Odalys's note suggest?
choices: Observation can matter as much as training
lines.hint: Not quite. Think about what she wrote beneath the map.
lines.correctText: Exactly. What you notice can matter as much as what you were taught.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Question 4: In the final paragraph, what does <color=red>observation</color> most nearly mean?
lines.hint: Not quite. Use the rest of the sentence as a clue.

lines.speaker: Tilly
lines.text: Flawless. You read with real <color=red>precision</color>. Four new books are arriving in the library as we speak.

afterLines.speaker: Tilly
afterLines.text: A pleasure, as always. Do go and see how the library's <color=red>collection</color> is coming along.
